name: Belnәng
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2019. Belnәng, an undocumented Chadic language of Central Nigeria. Draft circulated for comment, Jos, November 11, 2019. Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / rogerblench.info (retrieved via web.archive.org snapshot 20240724…
catalog_quote: 3.3 Tones Belnәng is a tone language with three level tones, low, middle and high. There are few glide tones. The following is a near-minimal triplet. sáár arm / ʃāār friend / sàr ten. Other pairs include; góŋ nose / gòŋ shoulder; pāār night / pààr vein

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote and locator verified verbatim in the PDF we hold (sec. 3.3, p. 5). The classification 'tonal, no stress statement' rests on a 2019 tentative sketch, but that sketch is the entire descriptive literature for this ~500-speaker language first reported in 2016: Glottolog has zero grammars/phonologies, and the only other substantive work (SIL JLSR 2021-026, downloaded now and read) disclaims any tone/phonology analysis and says nothing about stress. Three level tones with lexical minimal triplets is consistent with closely related A3 languages (Ngas, Mwaghavul). Not 'well-sourced' because the source is a self-described tentative draft with a three-paragraph phonology, but nothing better exists and nothing suggests the classification is wrong; no reclassification or re-read warranted.

sources.quote: No stress or prominence statement anywhere (0 hits for 'stress'). Appendix E, p. 34: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Wordlist items carry tone diacritics (e.g. pàŋ 'stone') but no accent marks; sections 6.3-6.5 compare segment inventories and sound correspondences with Ngas only.
